questions.stem: What is an Operational Reference Model needed for?
options: Scheduling batch jobs
Succeeding with metadata management by describing the structures and relationships of business metadata
Encrypting data at rest
Replacing the physical data model
Measuring network throughput
questions.explanation: To succeed with metadata management you need an Operational Reference Model, which describes the structures and relationships of your business metadata.

questions.stem: When do Operational Reference Models come into play?
options: When a single system needs a physical schema
When a project needs a communication diagram only
When organisations require an operational layer bridging multiple systems and functions with a common point of reference or shared language
When a database needs performance tuning
When a vendor requires a licence review
questions.explanation: Operational Reference Models provide an operational layer that bridges multiple systems and functions and gives the enterprise a shared language.

questions.stem: What distinguishes an Operational Reference Model from an anti-corruption layer or a semantic layer?
options: It is stored only in memory
It applies to a single system
It contains no metadata
It is owned and governed by the organisation's subject matter experts
It is maintained by the database vendor
questions.explanation: The Operational Reference Model is similar in purpose to an anti-corruption layer or semantic layer, but it is owned and governed by subject matter experts.

questions.stem: What is an Operational Reference Model at its core?
options: A collection of SQL views
A network diagram
A list of application servers
A set of business process flowcharts
A set of metadata structured with the help of taxonomies and ontologies
questions.explanation: At its core an Operational Reference Model is a set of metadata structured with the help of taxonomies and ontologies.

questions.stem: Which governance approach does an Operational Reference Model follow?
options: A federated governance approach in which each domain is governed by its subject matter experts
Centralised governance by the IT department alone
Governance outsourced to the database vendor
No governance, since the model is self-maintaining
Governance solely by the finance department
questions.explanation: Each domain is governed by the organisation's subject matter experts under a federated governance approach so IT, Business and Architects work in the same framework.

questions.stem: In Operational Reference Model governance, what is the role of IT?
options: Defining taxonomy levels within each domain
Providing a platform and/or database, plus a framework and interaction points such as integrations
Maintaining product-specific metadata
Defining the ontologies between taxonomies
Approving marketing campaigns
questions.explanation: IT acts as Platform Owner, providing the platform and/or database and the framework and interaction points, such as integrations, for using the metadata.

questions.stem: Which role is responsible in particular for defining the ontologies between different taxonomies?
options: IT (Platform Owner)
Subject Matter Experts
Architects (Structure Owner)
Finance
External auditors
questions.explanation: Architects, as Structure Owners, define the ontologies between taxonomies and ensure definitions are in place and attributes are named coherently.

questions.stem: Which three capabilities must a database have to implement an Operational Reference Model?
options: Full-text search, geospatial indexing and graph traversal
Sharding, replication and encryption
Column storage, compression and caching
Attribute inheritance, taxonomies (classification structures) and ontologies (relations)
Triggers, stored procedures and views
questions.explanation: Implementation requires a database that can manage attribute inheritance, taxonomies (classification structures) and ontologies (relations).

questions.stem: Why is attribute inheritance necessary in an Operational Reference Model?
options: To speed up query execution
To reduce storage costs
To allow vendor-specific extensions
To encrypt sensitive attributes
To ensure attributes are defined and used coherently without creating redundancy and ambiguity
questions.explanation: Attribute inheritance ensures attributes are defined and used in a coherent manner and do not create redundancy and ambiguity in their usage.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a listed benefit of an Operational Reference Model?
options: Eliminating the need for subject matter experts
Reducing time spent on new integrations
Enabling metadata quality through ownership by subject matter experts
Allowing analysis and simulations across abstraction levels
Maintaining a vendor-independent data layer that reduces lock-in
questions.explanation: An Operational Reference Model relies on subject matter experts for ownership and metadata quality; it does not eliminate them.
